rationale_overall: This week's pool is dominated by noise that does not clear the bar for a paired swap: a war-news cluster (Iran-UAE-Dubai missile/drone strikes, Gulf diplomatic calls, Syria airspace closure) is a pure geopolitical event story with no specific investable ticker attached, not a stock catalyst; 'Rocket League Championship' is an esports event, not aerospace; the Russian-missile-hits-Oreo-factory pieces are a keyword false-match on 'missile,' not a defense play; school/college robotics-team stories (St. Mary's, Decatur Christian, Texas Rocket Engineering Lab) are non-investable; Firehawk Aerospace and HD Hyundai's warship delivery involve a private US startup and a foreign (Korean) issuer respectively, neither a clean US-listed add; China's humanoid-robotics standard and India's QpiAI quantum chip are non-US-investable; IBM's vague India quantum/cloud investment note and the generic uranium-supercycle commentary lack a specific, non-mega-cap ticker with a concrete catalyst strong enough to displace an existing holding. The NVDA-specific items (Rubin chip timeline, Blackwell/DeepSeek chip story, earnings preview) and GOOGL's Gemini/robotics-in-house items are simply incremental due-diligence support for tickers already held, not new-add cases. Given the constraint that any add this period requires a paired remove, and nothing here is clearly a stronger rising-wave vehicle than GOOGL, NVDA, RKLB, or SMR, the watchlist is left unchanged this week.
